findings.item: OLBG-listed events against priced fixtures
findings.finding: The 20:32Z capture lists 127 events that start after the capture clock. The desk prices 83 fixtures across all sports, of which 42 were matched to an OLBG listing. Rows OLBG lists that the desk does not price are shown blank, not filled.

findings.item: Five written predictions per sport
findings.finding: 12 of 15 sports fall short of the five-a-sport target. Shortfall by sport: Baseball 4, Darts 2, Gaelic Sports 5, Golf 5, Greyhounds 5, Handball 1, Ice Hockey 2, Motor Racing 4, Rugby Union 4, Snooker 4, Tennis 4, Volleyball 2. No prediction was written for a selection below medium confidence, and none was invented to fill a quota.

findings.item: Fixtures with no OLBG listing in today's capture
findings.finding: 51 of 93 fixtures have no OLBG event with the same two sides in the captured pages (Baseball 1, Basketball 6, Cricket 2, Darts 4, Gaelic Sports 4, Golf 2, Greyhounds 2, Handball 4, Motor Racing 2, Rugby League 9, Rugby Union 1, Snooker 8, Tennis 4, Volleyball 2). They stay published with their official source link; none is claimed to be on OLBG.

findings.item: OLBG pages with no event payload
findings.finding: olbg_events_golf (HTTP 200); olbg_events_snooker (HTTP 200); olbg_golf (HTTP 200); olbg_home (HTTP 200); olbg_hub_golf (HTTP 200) returned a body with an empty tips array at 20:32Z, so no OLBG event could be read for golf. Golf fixtures therefore rest on the tours' own pages, not on an OLBG listing.

findings.item: Official pages that refused the capture job
findings.finding: 57 of 181 captured URLs returned a non-200 status ({"404": 48, "0": 2, "403": 6, "500": 1}). They are stored and published: a 403 or a login redirect is evidence, not a silent gap.

findings.item: Bodies truncated at the 300 kB cap
findings.finding: 32 captured bodies hit the 300,000-byte cap and are stored truncated (10 sports). Any table beyond the cut is not read.

findings.item: Capture bundles are transcribed readings, not stored bodies
findings.finding: The 25 files under data/cadence/captures/ record a URL, a timestamp and hand-shaped readings; they do not store the response body, status code or a hash. Their contents therefore cannot be re-derived by this session, and are treated as an assertion by the publishing session. Every fixture also carries an official URL that a reader can open.

findings.item: Mixed time bases in the stored data
findings.finding: The stored values are kept exactly as each source published them: a UTC instant for NHL, MLB and the NRL display, a bare 'local' or 'viewer-local' string for EuroLeague, the ATP schedule and cricket.com.au, and a date with no clock for 78 of the 122 graded picks. Where an instant exists the desk converts it once to the reader's zone and labels that conversion; where it does not, the source's own wording is shown and the row is left off the day-based summary rather than given a time it never had.

findings.item: OLBG's listed start disagrees with the official start
findings.finding: 1 of the matched fixtures carry an OLBG start more than an hour away from the official one. Both values are published side by side and neither is adjusted: nba-0022600099 (Basketball) 230 min apart, OLBG lists CHI Bulls @ MIL Bucks. The largest is an NBA game that OLBG shows as already under way at the capture clock (`expired:1` in its own payload) while the NBA page carries an 8:00 PM ET tip, so the two sources genuinely disagree and the desk does not pick a winner between them.

findings.item: A match inherited from the previous layer was paired to the wrong game
findings.finding: OLBG event 160789 (TB Rays @ MIL Brewers) starts 2026-10-24T00:00Z, which is MLB game 849805. The earlier reconciliation attached it to 849802, the same two teams one day later, because it accepted any pairing within 36 hours. This session requires the start to agree within twelve hours and takes the closest, so 849805 now carries the OLBG listing and 849802 is published as having no OLBG counterpart. The same rule dropped the Motor Racing match: OLBG's 'USA Grand Prix 2026' is listed 23 hours before the official race start, which is too far apart to call the same session.

The layers disagree, no note reconciles them, and none of the differences is explained by a published change of inputs. This desk publishes the cadence figure and records the others here rather than averaging them.

prior_layer_findings.finding: Written predictions exist for the graded selections listed on /cadence/predictions.html. prior_layer_findings.item: This desk is another overlapping dashboard
prior_layer_findings.finding: The repository already holds more than thirty desks covering the same brief. Adding /cadence/ makes that thirty-eight, and the ledger desk's own repository review flags the overlap as a high-severity finding (RR-02). /cadence/ is published in its own namespace, states its capture window and its shortfalls, and does not claim to supersede any other layer; a single authoritative desk is an integration decision, not a claim this session can make unilaterally.

prior_layer_findings.item: The two rules in the brief intersect in 1.43 percentage points
prior_layer_findings.finding: 'High confidence above 70%' and 'price between -250 and +10000' intersect only in 70.00%-71.43%, because a fair -250 is 71.43%. The desk therefore publishes each selection's own fair price and marks whether it is in band, and additionally quotes an alternate line at the band ceiling wherever a continuous line ladder exists. It never relabels a shorter price as in band. Today 0 of the 22 high-confidence selections are inside the band on their natural price (all 22 sit above 71.43%), 8 clear it on an alternate line set at the ceiling, and 14 are genuinely outside because they are outright or money-line markets with no ladder.
